goods.name: Pearls
goods.blurb: Beautiful deep-water pearls. Perfect for jewellery or a wedding gift.
goods.nature: Otters grow pearls in the shallow beds off Tassel's rafts and pick them by hand. A wedding needs three, so most of them never leave the water they grew in. Emberkin houses buy them thirty at a time.

goods.name: Tide glass
goods.blurb: Beautiful sea glass. Perfect for decoration or pressure vessels.
goods.nature: Otters forge tideglass in the volcanic trenches beneath Tassel's ocean. It is perfect for the underwater cities down in the cold depths. Other species simply find it beautiful.

goods.name: Moonfish oil
goods.blurb: Cheap and light. Keeps forever. Sells anywhere dark.
goods.nature: Pressed from a fish that only rises on the dark of the moon. Burns clean, keeps forever, and smells so exactly of a working harbour that people a long way from one buy a jar to open in the room.

goods.name: Coral carvings
goods.blurb: Dear and light. Otters pay most.
goods.nature: Cut from living reef and finished with a thumb: a year of somebody's evenings. They are given rather than sold, so one that reaches a market has usually come out of a household that broke up.

goods.name: Shiny moon pebbles
goods.blurb: Smooth grey moon rocks. No otter can walk past one.
goods.nature: Otters have been picking up shiny rocks since long before they had ships, and leaving the water has not cured it. These are offcuts, tumbled smooth in the Slate yards and swept off the floor by the crate. Every otter who buys one knows that, and buys one anyway.

goods.name: Iron ore
goods.blurb: Heavy and cheap. Smelters take all of it.
goods.nature: Nickel-iron, dug and sorted and nothing else done to it. Worthless until somebody with a furnace gets hold of it, and then worth whatever they make of it.

goods.name: Engraved masonry
goods.blurb: Heavy and cheap. Only builders want it.
goods.nature: Cut stone carrying the old patterns. Nothing lighter will hold a terrace up, and a terrace is expected to outlast the argument that built it.

goods.name: Medicinal herbs
goods.blurb: Light. Worth most where nothing grows.
goods.nature: Cut green and bundled in the field. Half the remedies in the system start here, and a physician can tell a wet-cut bundle from a good one by the squeak.

goods.name: Starfruit wine
goods.blurb: Light. Small runs, and the price swings.
goods.nature: Pale and faintly sharp, made in runs too small to matter to anyone except the people who cannot get any. Scarcity is most of the flavour and the growers know it.

goods.name: Glowmoss
goods.blurb: Cheap and light. Sells to anyone living underground.
goods.nature: A living lamp in a jar: needs nothing, never goes out, and does not mind being underground. Line a corridor with it and the corridor is faintly green forever.

goods.name: Rare riverfish
goods.blurb: Needs temperature control. Cats pay most.
goods.nature: Silver, quick, and out of three rivers only. One that arrives still cold is worth a month of parts. One that does not is worth an apology.

goods.name: Spare engine parts
goods.blurb: Heavy. Every dry dock is short of them.
goods.nature: Valves, seals and struts in oiled paper. Far from a dry dock, a crate of these is the difference between a ship and a wreck, which is why nobody far from a dry dock asks the price twice.

goods.name: Weapons
goods.blurb: Heavy and dear. Emberkin houses pay most.
goods.nature: Crated house arms, sealed with somebody's mark. There are feuds eleven years old that have never fired one and have never once stopped buying them.

goods.name: Heat-resistant plating
goods.blurb: Heavy. For hulls that go somewhere hot.
goods.nature: Sheet that will sit in a cloud top all day and come out grumbling. Half the shielded hulls in the sky are wearing it, including, if you have one, yours.

goods.name: Refined steel
goods.blurb: Heavy and dull. Always wanted.
goods.nature: Bar stock, graded and stamped. The dullest cargo in the system and the one everybody is short of, because nobody plans for it and everybody uses it.

goods.name: Reactor coils
goods.blurb: Hand-wound reactor coils. Perfect for a refit or a failing reactor.
goods.nature: Emberkin smiths on Cinder wind each coil by hand over nine days, in an order they have never written down. Nothing else will make a reactor behave. Cats will trade a whole ship for a crate of them.

goods.name: Fire crystals
goods.blurb: Needs temperature control. Dear, and the price swings.
goods.nature: Grown in the vents and cut cold, and they have to stay cold or they let go of it all at once. Kept properly, one holds a light for a week after the sun comes off it — enough to light a room and call it modesty.

goods.name: Volcanic glass
goods.blurb: Heavy and cheap. Four ports take it.
goods.nature: Black glass off the flows, packed in ash. Cheap wherever there is nothing else to sell, and cheap everywhere else because everybody has worked out that it cuts.

goods.name: Emberstone
goods.blurb: Light and dear. The price swings.
goods.nature: Still warm to the hand a year out of the ground, and nobody has ever explained why. The official position where it is mined is that it came out warm and will go back in warm. People sleep with them.

goods.name: Ember silk
goods.blurb: This season's colour sells double. Last season's is worthless.
goods.nature: It comes off the loom the colour of ash and takes the dye only above ninety degrees, so it is woven in a heated room by people paid very well to sweat. The season's colour turns over four times a year, and the dyers know the next one first.

goods.name: Faction medals
goods.blurb: Light and dear. Sells to people who want the name.
goods.nature: The metal is worth nothing. The name struck into it settles an argument in public, which in some houses is the only way an argument is accepted as settled.

goods.name: Precision clocks
goods.blurb: Otters pay most. A raft buys one together.
goods.nature: A second a month. On a world whose year runs fifty-six days that is the difference between a season and a mistake, and to a ship's navigator it is the difference between planning a launch window and guessing at one. Nobody else has the least use for it, which has never stopped anybody buying one.

goods.name: Perfume oils
goods.blurb: Light and dear. Four ports take it.
goods.nature: Distilled a drop at a time from flowers grown for nothing else, and cut with an oil that carries a scent without adding one of its own. A case holds twelve and weighs nothing. Most of what it costs is the four years it took to make the blend repeat.

goods.name: Storm crystals
goods.blurb: Very dear. One source only. Cats pay most.
goods.nature: Pulled off a cloud top on a line, still ticking. Nobody is certain what they are. People who are never quiet will hold one up to a lamp and go quiet.

goods.name: Advanced filters
goods.blurb: Heavy. Every sealed habitat needs them.
goods.nature: Patient, fine, and better than anything the inner worlds can build. The makers will explain exactly how, at length, twice, and you will still not be able to do it.

goods.name: Ancient cider
goods.blurb: Needs temperature control. Otters pay most.
goods.nature: Laid down in a balloon city ten thousand years ago, for drinkers who had not hatched yet. The cellar has been moved four times and never once opened in a hurry. People weep at it, and the makers consider weeping the correct response.

goods.name: Medicinal gel
goods.blurb: Needs temperature control. Everybody buys it.
goods.nature: Cold, clear, and it will close a wound that nothing else will. Warm it once and it is soup, which has happened to enough pilots that there is a word for them.

goods.name: Brine amber
goods.blurb: Dear and light. Only two ports take it.
goods.nature: Ammonia-sea amber with something inside it that is not a leaf: six arms, folded, and a seam down the middle that has been open and shut. Nothing in that sea has bones.

goods.name: Sea-foam resin
goods.blurb: Cheap and light. Fixes anything, sells anywhere.
goods.nature: Sets hard in vacuum and stays a little soft forever. A crate of this will fix almost anything, and whoever is fixing it will do it in front of you, at some length.

goods.name: Ice lenses
goods.blurb: Needs temperature control. Dear. Rich buyers only.
goods.nature: Ground from shell ice that has never once melted, and will not survive meeting anything that has. You can read a ship's name off one from further than you would believe.

goods.name: Cryo fuel
goods.blurb: Heavy bulk cryogenic fuel. Perfect for cold holds or smelters.
goods.nature: Frogs draw it from under the ice shell at Glass and ship it out in double-walled crates. Everything cold in the system runs on it. They think it is the dullest thing they make and are glad somebody wants it.

goods.name: Moon incense
goods.blurb: Light. Festival worlds pay most.
goods.nature: Rolled in silence by people who chose to live somewhere expensive to reach. It burns slow, travels badly, and most of what it costs is the getting there.

goods.name: Pilgrim beads
goods.blurb: Cheap. Worth more after a round trip.
goods.nature: Strung one a day for a year. A pilgrim carries them out and carries them back, and the ones that have been somewhere cost more than the ones that have not — the only market in the system that prices distance honestly.

goods.name: Ancient frog tea
goods.blurb: Very dear. Otters pay most.
goods.nature: Pressed into bricks longer ago than anybody was keeping records, by people who keep records. A brick is broken for a guest, and having one broken for you when you are only passing through is a considerable thing.

goods.name: Prayer lanterns
goods.blurb: Cheap and light. Sells at the turn of the year.
goods.nature: Paper and wire, with a wish folded inside where nobody reads it. They go up all at once at the turn of the year, and the sky above is unusable for about an hour.

goods.name: Festival dyes
goods.blurb: Cheap and light. Three ports take them.
goods.nature: Ground pigment in twists of waxed cloth. Cheap where they are made for a festival, and dear where somebody has worked out what else they will colour.

goods.name: Frogwood instruments
goods.blurb: Heavy and very dear. Only three ports take them.
goods.nature: Built from wood that grows on one terrace and tuned over a lifetime — the maker's, and then whoever gets it next. People constitutionally unable to stop talking stop talking.

goods.name: Salvaged ship plating
goods.blurb: Heavy scrap. Any yard takes it.
goods.nature: Whatever came off last, straightened and stacked by thickness. Every sheet was somebody's hull, and the yards that sell it do not mention whose: manners, they say, rather than superstition.

goods.name: Rebuilt thrusters
goods.blurb: Heavy and dear. Rebuilt sells close to new.
goods.nature: Stripped, cleaned, and put back together better than they were built, by somebody who mainly wanted to settle an argument about how they should have been built in the first place.

goods.name: Salvaged sensors
goods.blurb: Light. Cats pay most.
goods.nature: Working, mostly. The ones cut out of the ring see further than they are supposed to, and whoever pays for those is not pointing them at a shipping lane.

goods.name: Arc fragments
goods.blurb: The dearest cargo there is. Frogs and rich houses both.
goods.nature: A hand's length of seamless metal with no join, no tooling mark, and no way to tell which way up it is meant to go. It hums when you tap it — and so does every other piece ever cut off the ring, at the same note.

goods.name: Stolen Ember weapons
goods.blurb: Heavy and dear. Cats pay most.
goods.nature: House arms with the marks taken off badly; a thumb finds the filing. Selling them near where they came from means selling them back to the people they were taken from, at a markup.

goods.name: Counterfeit faction medals
goods.blurb: Cheap and light. Sells to the people it names.
goods.nature: Struck this morning and aged this afternoon. Good enough that the houses they name buy them, which is either very funny or the entire point, depending on which house you ask.

goods.name: Smuggled medicine
goods.blurb: Needs temperature control. Worth most where the real thing is priced out.
goods.nature: The same crates as the legitimate ones, at half the price, going to the three places that were priced out of the real thing. The apothecaries who brewed it know exactly where it went.

goods.name: Cybernetic body parts
goods.blurb: Very dear. Cats pay most.
goods.nature: Hands, eyes and spine, packed in gel and labelled in a hand that is not a doctor's. Somebody who has lost something to vacuum will pay anything and ask nothing.

cinder.name: Cinder
cinder.notes: Engine smiths; the cheapest fuel in the system straight from the refineries.

scorch.name: Scorch
scorch.notes: Mining frontier. Cheap rock, dangerous work, and the Emberkin nobody at home writes to.

veyra.name: Veyra
veyra.notes: Auction houses and money. Everything is for sale and everybody is watching who buys it.

tassel.name: Tassel
tassel.notes: The gossip hub and starting port. Big market, honest prices, terrible secrets.

slate.name: Slate
slate.notes: Dry docks and cranes. Tanks and holds are fitted here, as they are anywhere with a pump, and here they come with commentary.

moss.name: Moss
moss.notes: Farming moon, green to the shoreline. Will sell you grain and fruit and ask where you bank.

nail.name: Nail
nail.notes: Belt haven. Repairs, salvage and a bar. Match speeds and knock.

whisker.name: Whisker
whisker.notes: The shady end of the Belt. No questions, no paperwork, and a fitter who works in the dark.

arc.name: The Arc
arc.notes: Cat salvagers camped on the rim of a Builder ring, riding just beyond the Belt. No fuel; bring your own or beg.

grumm.name: Grumm
grumm.notes: Balloon cities in the cold upper clouds. The trade window for the whole frog system.

brine.name: Brine
brine.notes: Ammonia seas and floating apothecaries. Chemistry nobody else can read.

glass.name: Glass
glass.notes: Research station over an ocean under ice. They study the Builders and will talk your ear off.

croak.name: Croak
croak.notes: Retrograde and austere. Barely a market. The approach is dear on purpose.

haven.name: Haven
haven.notes: The frog capital and the outer system’s great market. No haggling; prices are exchange rates and goodwill.

maw.name: The Maw
maw.notes: No market. Something down there is still keeping station.

upgrades.name: Stock tank
upgrades.effect: The tank the ship came with (size from tuning).
upgrades.unlocks: Tassel's moons, the Belt, and a loose capture at Grumm.

upgrades.name: Long-haul tank
upgrades.unlocks: Cinder and the inward run, where the arrival is most of the bill.

upgrades.name: Deep-sky tank
upgrades.effect: Larger Δv budget again (size from tuning).
upgrades.unlocks: Grumm and Haven without counting every metre; the Arc with room to come home.

upgrades.name: Deep-dark tank
upgrades.unlocks: The Maw, and running hot anywhere you like.

upgrades.name: Stock hold
upgrades.effect: The hold the ship came with (units from tuning; the sim assumes 24).
upgrades.unlocks: One consignment at a time, and not a large one.

upgrades.name: Raft hold
upgrades.unlocks: Bulk runs that actually pay: ore and steel by the crate rather than the armful.

upgrades.name: Barge hold
upgrades.effect: Larger cargo capacity again (units from tuning).
upgrades.unlocks: A delivery and a speculation in the same hold.

upgrades.name: Barn hold
upgrades.unlocks: Ore and masonry by the barge, and a full frog gift-exchange in one trip.

upgrades.name: Gravitational sensors
upgrades.effect: See gravitational phenomena on the chart.
upgrades.unlocks: Nothing yet: the phenomena are not in the sky so far.

upgrades.name: Temperature control
upgrades.effect: The hold can carry goods that will not keep at hold temperature.
upgrades.unlocks: Rare riverfish, fire crystals, ancient cider, ice lenses, medicinal gel and smuggled medicine.

upgrades.name: The Astrolabe
upgrades.effect: Reads the transfer window to every world that goes round the Lamp: what a crossing would cost today, and how many days until it is cheap.
upgrades.unlocks: Interplanetary work. No harbourmaster will hand you a job that leaves their own sky without one.

upgrades.name: Heat shielding
upgrades.effect: Survive an atmosphere skim, at a risk.
upgrades.unlocks: Nothing yet: risky aerobraking is not built.

upgrades.name: Cryo hull cooling
upgrades.effect: Carries the heat of a skim away, so the skim is safe.
upgrades.unlocks: Nothing yet: safe aerobraking is not built.

price.description: You pay base * sells.priceMul * mood * (1 - repDiscount). A port pays base * demand * (needsTempControl ? tempControlMul : 1) * mood * (1 + repDiscount/2). Nothing else moves a price: what you have sold here before does not, and how picked-over a shelf is does not. The stall's stock is the only limit on how much of a thing you can move at once, and that is limit enough.

reputation.description: Reputation is 0..10 points per species. Purchases and fuel at that species' ports are discounted by min(maxDiscount, discountPerPoint*points). Frog gifts scale with frog reputation; cat tolls fall by the same fraction.

toll.description: A Belt toll intercept takes min(cap, fraction*cargoValue) in goods, chosen by the cats; nothing if cargoValue < minCargoValue (they never take everything and never harm a ship that yields). There is nothing to hide behind: the only let-off is the cooldown, so a captain is never asked twice inside a month.

tow.description: A stranded or crashed ship is towed to the nearest port: cost = base + perAu*distanceAu, time = max(3, daysPerAu*distanceAu) days. If you cannot pay, the Tassel harbour bank fronts it and the debt is deducted from sales.

haggle.description: Otter ports: each visit rolls a uniform spread of +-spread on every price, then a haggle mini-exchange lets you keep the good end of the roll. Frogs never haggle (spread 0). Cats and Emberkin do not haggle either.

volatility.description: Daily random-walk wobble on what a port pays, amplitude by species. Emberkin markets are the most volatile. This is species character, not supply and demand: it does not remember anything you did.

speciesRules.otter: Haggle spread: every price at an otter port is rolled within +-spread, per good, per day. The roll is the whole of it — there is no haggling exchange behind it.
speciesRules.emberkin: Volatile prices: what Cinder wants this week is not what it wanted last week.
speciesRules.cat: Tolls in the Belt under strict custom (never everything, never a ship that yields). Impress a captain and a gift may follow.
speciesRules.frog: No haggling. "Prices" are exchange rates: you are paid in trade credit at the stall plus goodwill (reputation), and every visit ends with a gift.

stock.description: A stall's shelves hold a number rolled out of the good's own stock range, and they are rolled again when you come back from somewhere else. Staying at one dock and waiting does not restock it; going and trading elsewhere does. What you bought this visit is what is missing, and the price does not move as the shelf empties: the shelf itself is the limit.

demand.description: What a port pays for a good, as a multiple of its base price. Two questions: does this port want it (loved, on its buyer list, or neither), and is it out of the good's own region. Space is hard and there are few interspecies merchants, so carrying a loved good to another people is the trade the game is about; the same run inside one system is worth a fraction of it. Regions are named in the ports table: inner, home, belt, outer, deep.

sim.notes: orbitAu per port is the circular radius used for straight-line distance and Hohmann estimates; moons quote their parent’s radius.

regions.inner: The Emberkin worlds: Cinder, Scorch and Veyra.
regions.home: Tassel and its moons, Slate and Moss.
regions.belt: The Belt: Nail, Whisker and the Arc.
regions.outer: Grumm and its moons: Brine, Glass, Croak and Haven.
